meta.source: WP06_enhanced.md (cooling architecture), WP09_enhanced.md (node analysis, CyHAZOPs hazard logs), WP10_enhanced.md (ALE / ROSI); WP16_ConOps_MOR.md (operating modes, MoR registers); WP08_Fat_Tail_Risk.md (MITRE mapping)
meta.role: Authored redundancy, timing thresholds, failure modes and consequence values. Overrides anything the model infers.
meta.note: RPN-C = severity x occurrence-cyber x detection-cyber, per the CyHAZOPs method in WP09. MITRE identifiers are ATT&CK for ICS technique IDs.

cell_structure.cell_mw_range: 5-10 MW power/cooling block, deployed and operated independently
cell_structure.isolation: Cell-level isolation creates IEC 62443 zones inherently. A compromise in one cell does not propagate to another provided the cells are on separate OT segments with no shared management plane.

modelled_cell.note: The model contains TWO cells of 48 racks each (rows 01-03 = Cell A, rows 04-06 = Cell B). At 6.91 MW total load per cell this sits inside the stated 5-10 MW band. Campus figures are one cell multiplied by the cell count.

cell_structure.cells_per_campus_note: 100 MW campus / 6.91 MW total load per cell = 14.5 cells. An earlier revision used 8.7, which came from treating the whole 96-rack hall as one cell.

revenue_basis.correction: Two corrections. (1) An earlier revision divided the whole 100 MW campus revenue across 96 racks, giving $130K/rack-hour — the cell basis gives $15K/rack-hour. (2) The 96-rack hall was then treated as a single 11.52 MW cell, above the stated 5-10 MW band; it is two cells of 48 racks, so per-cell consequence halves and the campus cell count rises from 8.7 to 14.5.
revenue_basis.scope_note: WP10 node ALEs are campus-wide worst case (all cells affected). Cell isolation is the control that prevents that. A single-cell event is roughly 1/14.5 of the WP10 figure. Report both. The N2 and N8 ratios landing on exactly 8.7 against the old single-cell reading was an artefact of the wrong cell size, not confirmation.

coverage.note: WP09 provides worked hazard logs for six nodes; N2, N5 and N6 are transcribed. N8, N10 and N14 have ALE and controls but no hazard rows yet.

reconciliation.reading: WP10 assumes every cell loses UPS simultaneously — the shared-management-plane case cell isolation is designed to prevent.
Closest to single-cell scale; central chiller plant is genuinely shared across cells, so partial campus impact is credible.
WP10 values 16 rack-hours at $390K/rack-hour. Either the GPU damage is double-counted in the revenue line, or the outage is wider than 8 racks. Worth resolving at source.
Explicitly campus-wide — a single BMS serving all cells. If BMS is per-cell as WP06 states, this is 1/8.7 per cell.

unit_priced.safeguard: Specify SL-2 certified NMC in procurement; valid
VFD Modbus write-enable gated by a physical keys

safeguard_summary.note: WP09 Tables 9.4 and 9.7 price safeguards per hazard. These are hazard-level remediations; the WP10 controls block is the portfolio view. Some are unit-priced (per VFD, per battery string) so campus totals depend on quantities.
safeguard_summary.systemic_finding: WP09 conclusion: protocol-level insecurity of BACnet/IP and Modbus TCP is the single greatest systemic risk across all nodes. Telemetry integrity (SPOOFED) produces the highest cyber RPNs.

protective_model.statement: Instrument assets carry a protective field. In the cascade they report as PROTECTION LOST rather than stopped: they sense load, they do not carry it.
protective_model.rationale: Without this distinction a 46-asset instrument layer would either look consequence-free or would wrongly propagate load loss through sensing paths, overstating the consequence of any power failure.

N5.label: Central chiller plant and heat rejection

node_crosswalk.N8: Supply chain, receiving and staging — EN 50600-2-5 zone G (System 21-22)
node_crosswalk.N10: Z6 untrusted / uncontrolled — external pathways into the facility (SaaS/B2B, tenant pods, vendor remote access, vendor telemetry)
node_crosswalk._confirm: Crosswalk proposed from the WP09 node descriptions — confirm before relying on the ALE figures.
node_crosswalk.N7: Lighting and emergency illumination (reference architecture System 12)
node_crosswalk.N9: Fire water supply, suppression availability and agent discharge control (HLD System 09 / Fire Suppression)

redundancy._rule: Authored from WP06 Table 6.5 and the WP09 critical items lists. Overrides the feed-count inference in the cascade.

row01_cdu.note: Row CDU is a single unit with internal N+1 pumps. Internal redundancy does not survive loss of the unit, so the row has no fallback.

timing.note: At densities above 80 kW/rack a CDU pump failure throttles GPUs within 45 s and forces protective shutdown within 90 s. Air cooling at 20 kW/rack provides minutes, not seconds.

hazards.deviation: All UPS blocks offline simultaneously
hazards.cyber_cause: Ransomware encrypts all NMC firmware via shared VLAN
hazards.consequence: Total IT load loss; generator start delay 10-15 s

hazards.deviation: All blocks forced to bypass simultaneously
hazards.cyber_cause: Attacker sends bypass command via Modbus TCP to all NMCs
hazards.consequence: IT load on raw utility power; no UPS protection

hazards.deviation: False battery state-of-charge reporting
hazards.cyber_cause: Attacker modifies SOC register to report 100% when depleted
hazards.consequence: Operator believes backup is available; next utility event drops the load

hazards.deviation: Overcharge of Li-ion battery string
hazards.cyber_cause: Attacker modifies charge voltage setpoint via BMS Modbus
hazards.consequence: Thermal runaway; fire; toxic gas; EPO activation

hazards.deviation: NMC firmware contains persistent implant
hazards.cyber_cause: Supply chain compromise of NMC firmware image
hazards.consequence: Implant survives factory reset; persistent access The card is now modelled as a discrete asset (ups_nmc), so this implant has an addressable landing point with its own command path into the UPS and the battery string.
hazards.resolved_note: Landing asset added from the BMS block diagram: ups_nmc, reachable from the shared L2 switch over SNMP v3.

hazards.deviation: All CHW pumps offline
hazards.cyber_cause: Attacker sends stop command to all pump VFDs via Modbus TCP
hazards.consequence: Zero cooling capacity; GPU throttling in 2-5 min; shutdown in 10-15 min

hazards.deviation: Supply temperature raised above design basis
hazards.cyber_cause: Attacker modifies chiller leaving water setpoint from 7 C to 20 C
hazards.consequence: Insufficient cooling; CDUs cannot maintain TCS temperature; gradual thermal drift

hazards.deviation: Operator sees 7 C while actual is 20 C
hazards.cyber_cause: Attacker intercepts BACnet sensor value; spoofs normal reading to BMS
hazards.consequence: Operator unaware of thermal drift; damage occurs before detection

hazards.deviation: All chillers tripped AND cooling tower fans disabled
hazards.cyber_cause: Simultaneous BACnet commands to chiller controllers and tower VFDs
hazards.consequence: Complete loss of heat rejection; campus-wide thermal emergency

hazards.deviation: Chillers unloaded during peak demand
hazards.cyber_cause: Attacker modifies plant optimiser demand signal
hazards.consequence: Capacity removed when most needed; thermal excursion during peak AI training load

hazards.deviation: BMS reads artificially low return temperature while actual supply temperature rises
hazards.cyber_cause: Attacker writes to CDU Modbus holding registers; BMS has no independent measurement to validate against
hazards.consequence: BMS reduces chiller output, amplifying the thermal excursion instead of correcting it; GPU throttling begins before the independent high-temperature trip fires
hazards.note: Highest cyber RPN in the WP09 hazard log; cyber multiplier 13.4x over the mechanical equivalent. Telemetry integrity is the controlling security property.

hazards.deviation: Generator shaft vibration interlock disabled or bypassed
hazards.cyber_cause: Physical access to the interlock wiring, or an engineering-workstation compromise that reconfigures the genset controller to ignore the trip input.
hazards.mitre: T0839 Module Firmware, T0836 Modify Parameter
hazards.consequence: Generator runs to mechanical destruction on a bearing or shaft fault. Loss of the unit removes N+1 backup generation for the duration of the repair, with a multi-month lead time on a 2.5 MW set.
hazards.source: Derived from TET-PWR-PID-001 Section 1 (VT-001, shutdown interlock) against WP09 node N2.

hazards.deviation: Transformer winding temperature signal spoofed low, defeating the trip
hazards.cyber_cause: Compromise of the 4-20 mA loop or the relay configuration so an overtemperature never reaches the trip threshold.
hazards.mitre: T0832 Manipulation of View, T0855 Unauthorized Command Message
hazards.consequence: Transformer runs beyond its thermal limit with no alarm and no trip. Insulation failure destroys the unit and drops the LV board it feeds — one of two supply paths to the whole hall.
hazards.source: Derived from TET-PWR-PID-001 Section 1 (TT-001, alarm and trip) against WP09 node N2.

hazards.deviation: ATS source qualification sensing lost, stranding load on a failed source
hazards.cyber_cause: Loss or falsification of VS-001 so the transfer switch does not recognise that its preferred source has failed.
hazards.mitre: T0832 Manipulation of View, T0814 Denial of Service
hazards.consequence: No transfer to generator on a utility failure. The UPS carries the load to battery exhaustion — 5 to 15 minutes — then the hall drops.
hazards.source: Derived from TET-PWR-PID-001 Section 2 (VS-001, ST-001) against WP09 node N2.

hazards.deviation: Battery state of charge reported higher than actual
hazards.cyber_cause: Modbus RTU spoofing on the SOC monitor, or firmware manipulation of the battery monitoring head-end.
hazards.mitre: T0832 Manipulation of View, T0856 Spoof Reporting Message
hazards.consequence: Operators and the automatic transfer logic believe autonomy exists that does not. A generator start is deferred past the real battery limit and the load drops without warning.
hazards.source: Derived from TET-PWR-PID-001 Section 2 (SOC-001) against WP09 node N2.

hazards.deviation: Day tank level reported higher than actual during an extended outage
hazards.cyber_cause: Spoofed 4-20 mA level signal or compromise of the tank gauge controller.
hazards.mitre: T0832 Manipulation of View, T0856 Spoof Reporting Message
hazards.consequence: Fuel replenishment is not dispatched. Generators run dry mid-outage; the facility loses all generation with the utility already down.
hazards.source: Derived from TET-PWR-PID-001 Section 1 (LT-001) against WP09 node N1.

hazards.deviation: PDU and rack energy metering falsified low
hazards.cyber_cause: Modbus TCP manipulation between the energy meters and DCIM, or compromise of the DCIM collector itself.
hazards.mitre: T0832 Manipulation of View, T0855 Unauthorized Command Message
hazards.consequence: Branch circuit overload is hidden until a breaker trips. PUE reporting is corrupted, and capacity decisions are made against understated load — an integrity attack with a commercial as well as an operational effect.
hazards.source: Derived from TET-PWR-PID-001 Sections 3 and 4 (EM-001, EM-002, WT-001) against WP09 node N3.

hazards.deviation: Protection relay commanded to trip the MV breaker on demand
hazards.cyber_cause: Compromise of the protection relay, or IEC 61850 GOOSE injection on the station bus, reached from the shared Purdue L2 managed switch.
hazards.mitre: T0855 Unauthorized Command Message, T0804 Block Reporting Message, T0836 Modify Parameter
hazards.consequence: Attacker-initiated loss of the MV supply. Both cells transfer to generator; if the transfer is also degraded the whole hall drops. This is the highest-authority write path in the electrical system and it is reachable from the same switch that carries cooling control.
hazards.source: Resolved from the power P&ID (Breaker Trip Control) and the BMS diagram (managed switch to protection relays). Confirmed shared-L2 topology.

hazards.deviation: UPS network management card used to force transfer, shutdown or bypass
hazards.cyber_cause: SNMP v3 credential compromise, or exploitation of the card web UI, from the shared L2 switch. Vendor firmware, infrequently patched.
hazards.mitre: T0839 Module Firmware, T0855 Unauthorized Command Message, T0814 Denial of Service
hazards.consequence: The card holds command authority over the UPS without any compromise of the UPS itself, and polls the battery string. Reaching four blocks reproduces N2-CY-001 and N2-CY-002 from a single network foothold, and an implant survives UPS maintenance.
hazards.source: Resolved from the BMS diagram (managed switch to UPS Network Mgmt Card, SNMP v3 / Modbus TCP).

hazards.deviation: Shared Purdue L2 managed switch compromise reaches electrical AND cooling controls
hazards.cyber_cause: Compromise of the industrial managed switch, or of any supervisory host attached to it — EPMS server, DCIM, historian, operator HMI.
hazards.mitre: T0842 Network Sniffing, T0830 Adversary-in-the-Middle, T0855 Unauthorized Command Message
hazards.consequence: Confirmed topology: one Purdue L2 managed switch carries all five control legs the BMS diagram draws — protection relay polling (IEC 61850 MMS / Modbus TCP), UPS network management card command (SNMP v3), chiller plant control (BACnet/IP), genset controller dispatch (Modbus TCP) and the six row CDU PLCs (Modbus TCP). A single switch compromise therefore spans both the electrical and the cooling system — the blast radius is the whole facility control layer, not one system.
hazards.source: Confirmed by the client against the BMS network block diagram. Not an inference.
hazards.verification: Query: walk forward from ot_sw over the routable protocol set. All five legs are direct outbound edges of ot_sw; no leg is asserted transitively.

hazards.deviation: DALI gateway used to extinguish or dim emergency luminaires
hazards.cyber_cause: Compromise of the DALI/BACnet gateway from the shared Purdue L2 switch, then a scene write to the emergency groups. Self-test records in the BMS historian falsified to hide failed luminaires.
hazards.mitre: T0855 Unauthorized Command Message, T0832 Manipulation of View, T0831 Manipulation of Control
hazards.consequence: A dark data hall with live 415 V busway overhead and no marked escape route, during the exact conditions that caused the evacuation. NFPA 101 requires 0.6 fc average after 90 minutes; a gateway write can defeat that without touching a single luminaire.
hazards.source: Reference architecture System 12 (IEC 62386 DALI-2, NFPA 101 7.9) against the confirmed shared-L2 topology.
hazards.note: The FACP hardwired scene trigger is the compensating control — facp to dali_ctl bypasses the gateway.

hazards.deviation: PA/VA used to suppress an evacuation or issue a false lockdown
hazards.cyber_cause: Compromise of the voice alarm control unit, or of the operator position that holds all-call authority.
hazards.mitre: T0855 Unauthorized Command Message, T0856 Spoof Reporting Message
hazards.consequence: Occupants either are not told to leave a building that is on fire, or are directed to shelter in the area of the hazard. This is the only system in the model whose compromise directly harms people rather than equipment, and EN 54-16 fire-voice priority is the control that must not be overridable.
hazards.source: Reference architecture System 13 (EN 54-16, NFPA 72 Ch.24).

hazards.deviation: Unverified hardware enters the estate with a legitimate asset record
hazards.cyber_cause: Compromise of the receiving WMS terminal or the burn-in segment, then a falsified goods receipt into the enterprise estate so the device arrives in the hall with an approved install ticket.
hazards.mitre: T0862 Supply Chain Compromise, T0873 Project File Infection, T0839 Module Firmware
hazards.consequence: Implanted hardware reaches Zone F through the front door, carrying paperwork. The burn-in rack runs unverified firmware on a live segment by design, so the attacker has a foothold before the device is ever racked. The staging VLAN is a deliberate stub, which bounds the network path — but not the physical one.
hazards.source: Reference architecture System 21-22 and EN 50600-2-5 zone G. Zone G was absent from the model before this revision.
hazards.verification: Query: threat walk from staging_sw reaches 293 assets. That is NOT a segmentation failure — the only outbound edge is internet egress, and the walk re-enters through the carrier perimeter like any external attacker. The direct inward path is genuinely absent. The physical path through the staging airlock is the one segmentation cannot bound, which is why the safeguard is firmware attestation rather than a firewall rule.

hazards.deviation: Unescorted movement from the loading dock into a data hall
hazards.cyber_cause: Credential elevation on the access control application so a dock badge also opens the staging airlock, or tailgating with the airlock camera disabled.
hazards.mitre: T0803 Block Command Message, T0814 Denial of Service
hazards.consequence: Defeats the single control the reference architecture requires between zone G and zone F. A delivery driver reaches the rack floor. The compensating evidence is the airlock camera, so disabling that first is the natural precursor.
hazards.source: EN 50600-2-5 zone G: no unescorted path from dock to data hall.

hazards.deviation: Chilled water buffer isolated without stopping a pump
hazards.cyber_cause: BACnet write from the BMS head-end closing the buffer isolation valve.
hazards.mitre: T0855 Unauthorized Command Message, T0836 Modify Parameter
hazards.consequence: Every cooling timeline shortens at once and nothing alarms, because no pump stopped and no temperature has moved yet. The first indication is a faster-than-expected rise after a subsequent plant trip — by which point the ride-through the operators are counting on is gone.
hazards.source: Reference architecture vertical stack, basement L2-L3 thermal buffer.

hazards.deviation: Sprinkler system isolated or discharging without the panel knowing
hazards.cyber_cause: Physical tamper on the riser control valve with the flow and tamper switch defeated, or loss of the hardwired supervisory contact.
hazards.mitre: T0878 Alarm Suppression, T0814 Denial of Service
hazards.consequence: A closed riser valve looks identical to a healthy system at the fire panel. Suppression is unavailable for the one event it exists to handle. NFPA 72 makes the tamper switch a supervisory initiating device precisely because this failure is otherwise silent.
hazards.source: Reference architecture System 09 and NFPA 13/20/22.

hazards.deviation: Spurious clean-agent discharge commanded or induced
hazards.cyber_cause: Compromise of the releasing panel, or forcing both detection zones to alarm so cross-zoning confirms. The panel is BACnet-visible for status, which is the reconnaissance path even though release authority is not networked.
hazards.mitre: T0855 Unauthorized Command Message, T0831 Manipulation of Control, T0878 Alarm Suppression
hazards.consequence: Irreversible. The agent dumps, HVAC shuts down and the EPO trips, so the hall is de-energised and unavailable until the agent is replaced and the space re-certified. Cost is the refill plus the outage, and there is no undo — unlike almost every other action in this model.
hazards.source: HLD Fire Suppression — Clean Agent. The releasing panel was absent from the scene until this revision.
hazards.note: Cross-zoning is the designed defence: one faulty or spoofed zone must not release.

hazards.deviation: Abort stations defeated, removing the human veto
hazards.cyber_cause: Physical tamper or wiring failure on the hold-to-abort circuits. No network path exists, so this is a maintenance and supervision failure rather than a remote attack.
hazards.mitre: T0814 Denial of Service
hazards.consequence: A person still in the hall when the countdown starts has no way to stop the discharge. This is the only control in the model whose loss directly endangers someone present, and its failure is silent until the moment it is needed.
hazards.source: NFPA 2001 abort switch requirement.

hazards.deviation: Vendor remote engineer endpoint used as the entry into the OT estate
hazards.cyber_cause: Compromise of a vendor-managed laptop that services many facilities, then a maintenance session through the jumpbox into chiller, UPS or genset controllers.
hazards.mitre: T0822 External Remote Services, T0866 Exploitation of Remote Services, T0859 Valid Accounts
hazards.consequence: The best-documented OT compromise route there is, and the model previously had no asset for it. Vendor endpoint hygiene is unverifiable from inside the facility, so the jumpbox is the only real control. A standing tunnel is a standing breach.
hazards.source: Z6 untrusted zone. Equipment outside operator administrative control with a pathway in.

hazards.deviation: SaaS / B2B partner path used to reach the enterprise estate
hazards.cyber_cause: Compromise of a partner endpoint or theft of API credentials held at the partner end, outside operator key management.
hazards.mitre: T0862 Supply Chain Compromise, T0859 Valid Accounts
hazards.consequence: A business-process path into the estate that no facility control governs, and one commonly exempted from OT change control because it is "just business systems". It is the same estate the industrial DMZ is meant to protect.
hazards.source: Z6 untrusted zone.

hazards.deviation: Compromised customer device reaches the shared spine fabric
hazards.cyber_cause: A tenant endpoint of unknown patch state, authenticated but not attested, escaping its VRF.
hazards.mitre: T0867 Lateral Tool Transfer, T0842 Network Sniffing
hazards.consequence: Many untrusted endpoints reach BOTH spines by design, so tenant VRF isolation is the only thing between one customer device and the fabric every other tenant shares.
hazards.source: Z6 untrusted zone.

mor.minimum: All transfer switches functional; tested within 90 days
mor.ot_requirement: Controller firmware integrity verified; transfer time under 10 ms confirmed
Chiller controller communication confirmed; setpoints within design range

mor.minimum: Sufficient heat rejection for N chiller load

safeguards.safeguard: Isolate NMCs on a dedicated management VLAN; segment blocks A/B onto separate VLANs
Independent battery monitoring not via the NMC; physical battery load test schedule
Hardwired BMS overvoltage protection relay (SIL-2), independent of the software setpoint
safeguards.note: SIL-2 hardwired — survives compromise of the setpoint path.

safeguards.safeguard: Specify SL-2 certified NMC in procurement; validate firmware hash against vendor baseline
VFD Modbus write-enable gated by a physical keyswitch; remote write disabled by default
Independent hardwired temperature alarm at CDU intake, bypassing the BMS, alerting the NOC directly
safeguards.note: Directly answers the SPOOFED guide word: an out-of-band measurement the attacker cannot write to.

safeguards.safeguard: Chiller plant and cooling towers on separate OT VLANs so compromise of one cannot reach the other
Manual chiller staging override physically available at the plant room panel, not network-accessible
Hardwire the vibration interlock direct to the genset trip circuit with no controller in the path, and prove the trip on each NFPA 110 exercise.
safeguards.basis: 3 generators x $6K interlock verification and wiring segregation

safeguards.safeguard: Dual independent winding temperature paths per transformer, with a discrepancy alarm; relay trip settings under configuration management.
safeguards.basis: 2 transformers x $12K second sensing path plus relay config baseline

safeguards.safeguard: Cross-check ATS source qualification against the EPMS bus voltage reading, and alarm on divergence for more than 2 seconds.
safeguards.basis: EPMS logic and alarm engineering across 2 ATS units

safeguards.safeguard: Serial-to-IP gateway with Modbus function-code allow-listing on the battery monitoring path; SOC cross-checked against measured string voltage.
safeguards.basis: 2 gateways x $12K plus $8K monitoring logic

safeguards.safeguard: Independent mechanical sight-gauge reading logged per shift during any generator run, treated as the authoritative fuel figure.
safeguards.basis: procedural control plus 3 gauge installations

safeguards.safeguard: Read-only Modbus TCP from the metering layer to DCIM through a unidirectional gateway; reconcile monthly against the revenue meter.
safeguards.basis: 1 unidirectional gateway at $38K plus $7K reconciliation tooling

safeguards.safeguard: IEC 61850 GOOSE authentication and a relay settings-change baseline under configuration management; deny relay settings access from the shared L2 VLAN, permit only from a dedicated protection engineering VLAN.
safeguards.basis: 2 relay lineups, VLAN redesign and settings baselining
safeguards.source: Power P&ID Breaker Trip Control / BMS diagram L2 to L1

safeguards.safeguard: Dedicated UPS management VLAN, SNMP v3 authPriv only with no v1/v2c fallback, card web UI disabled, and firmware inventory tracked against vendor advisories.
safeguards.basis: 4 cards x $4K hardening plus $12K VLAN and monitoring work
safeguards.source: BMS diagram Purdue L1 (AP9641 / Vertiv class)

safeguards.safeguard: Split the shared L2 switch into separate electrical and cooling VLANs with an inspecting boundary between them, so a compromise of one control domain cannot reach the other.
safeguards.basis: switch replacement, VLAN redesign, boundary firewall and re-commissioning of both control domains
safeguards.source: Confirmed shared-L2 topology — the single largest architectural finding

safeguards.safeguard: Emergency luminaire groups addressed on a DALI line the gateway cannot write, driven only by the FACP hardwired scene contact; self-test records mirrored to an append-only store outside the BMS.
safeguards.basis: separate DALI line, hardwired scene wiring, append-only log target

safeguards.safeguard: EN 54-16 fire-voice priority enforced in the VACU firmware and verified at commissioning; all-call authority limited to the physical SOC microphone with no network path.
safeguards.basis: commissioning verification plus removal of the network command path

safeguards.safeguard: Firmware attestation at burn-in against a vendor-signed manifest, with the goods receipt gated on a passing attestation rather than on a scan.
safeguards.basis: attestation tooling, manifest ingest, WMS workflow change

safeguards.safeguard: Anti-tailgating turnstile at the staging airlock with the camera as an interlock rather than a record — no release while the view is obscured or the feed is lost.
safeguards.basis: turnstile, camera analytics, interlock wiring

safeguards.safeguard: Buffer isolation valve position alarmed independently of the BMS command path, with a discrepancy alarm between commanded and sensed position.
safeguards.basis: independent position sensing and alarm logic

safeguards.safeguard: Riser valve tamper switches on a supervised NFPA 72 circuit with end-of-line monitoring, tested quarterly against a deliberate valve close.
safeguards.basis: supervised circuit conversion and test procedure

safeguards.safeguard: Releasing panel on a dedicated NFPA 72 releasing circuit with no shared I/O; BACnet status path read-only and physically separate from the release logic; cross-zone confirmation verified at every annual test.
safeguards.basis: circuit segregation, read-only status gateway, annual verification procedure

safeguards.safeguard: Abort circuits supervised end-of-line with a trouble annunciation at the panel, tested quarterly by actual hold rather than by continuity alone.
safeguards.basis: supervised circuit conversion on 2 stations plus test procedure

safeguards.safeguard: Operator-initiated, time-boxed, session-recorded vendor access only. No standing tunnels; jumpbox posture check and per-session approval with an automatic expiry.
safeguards.basis: PAM session broker, recording, approval workflow

safeguards.safeguard: Terminate every partner session in the industrial DMZ with no traverse; partner credentials rotated on an operator-held schedule and integration traffic brought inside OT change control.
safeguards.basis: DMZ termination, credential rotation, change-control scope extension

safeguards.safeguard: Per-tenant VRF enforced at both spines with an explicit deny between tenant VRFs, and endpoint attestation before pod access is granted.
safeguards.basis: dual-spine VRF policy plus attestation gateway

assumptions.statement: The model contains 96 racks at 120 kW = 11.52 MW IT, 13.82 MW at PUE 1.2. The stated cell band is 5-10 MW, so the model is 1.4-2.8x one cell. Half the hall (48 racks, 5.76 MW IT / 6.91 MW total) sits squarely in band.
assumptions.consequence: Every per-cell consequence figure is currently computed over 96 racks. If a cell is 48 racks, all cell-scoped losses halve and the campus cell count rises from 8.7 to ~14.5.
assumptions.resolution: Resolved: the hall is two cells of 48 racks (6.91 MW each), not one of 11.52 MW. Per-cell figures halved; campus cell count 14.5.

assumptions.statement: WP10 gives 100 MW and $12.5M/hr but does not say whether 100 MW is IT load or total facility power.
assumptions.consequence: IT load basis gives $125K/MW-hr and $15K/rack-hour. Total-facility basis (83 MW IT at PUE 1.2) gives $150K/MW-hr and $18K/rack-hour, 20% higher.
assumptions.resolution: Confirm the denominator. The model uses the conservative IT-load basis.

assumptions.statement: WP09/WP10 node IDs were mapped to model asset ids by description. N2 to the four UPS blocks plus batteries and STS, N5 to chillers and towers, N6 to the six CDUs and their PLCs, N8 to the BMS platforms, N10 to the fire system, N14 to rack BMCs.
assumptions.consequence: Every ALE and hazard attribution hangs off this mapping.
assumptions.resolution: Review graph/hazard-log.json meta.node_crosswalk against the source papers.

assumptions.statement: Six assets carry authored redundancy from WP06 Table 6.5. Everything else infers redundancy from inbound feed count: two or more feeds of a service hold, one does not.
assumptions.consequence: Inferred redundancy may be optimistic where a load genuinely requires both feeds rather than either.
assumptions.resolution: Extend REDUNDANCY_OVERRIDE from the DLD single-line diagrams.

assumptions.statement: Threat paths follow the direction of initiated sessions, not physical adjacency. The ToR management plane was made bidirectional on instruction, since a compromised host can initiate back up its own uplink.
assumptions.consequence: Bidirectional traversal of all edges reported 127 assets reachable from guest Wi-Fi, making segmentation look worthless. Session-direction traversal is the defensible reading.

assumptions.statement: Where several controls address one scenario the model reports the highest single mitigation rate rather than the product.
assumptions.consequence: Conservative. Compounding would overstate the benefit of overlapping controls.

assumptions.statement: WP09 claims worked hazard logs for six nodes but contains CY-numbered rows for N2 and N5 only, plus one N6 entry recovered from a field observation. N8, N10 and N14 have ALE and controls but no hazard rows.
assumptions.consequence: Those three nodes cannot be seeded from hazards, only from assets.
assumptions.resolution: Complete during a live engagement, as WP09 itself states.

assumptions.statement: The model places three chillers and two towers as if dedicated to this hall. WP06 describes the central chiller plant as shared across cells, which is why the N5 reconciliation came out at 2.9x rather than 8.7x.
assumptions.consequence: A chiller failure in the model stops only this hall. In reality it would degrade several cells.
assumptions.resolution: Either scope the chiller plant as campus-shared, or confirm per-cell chiller clusters.

assumptions.statement: TET-PWR-PID-001 gives ranges rather than selections — transformers 500 to 2,500 kVA, UPS 100 to 1,000 kVA, battery autonomy 5 to 15 minutes, generators 2.5 MW per unit. The model carries the mid-range figure in each case.
assumptions.consequence: Consequence timing is sensitive to battery autonomy in particular: at 5 minutes rather than 15, the window between a utility loss and a load drop is three times shorter, which changes whether a transfer failure is recoverable.
assumptions.resolution: Replace with the selected equipment ratings from the facility submittal register at the next floor walk.

assumptions.statement: TET-PWR-PID-001 is a generic hyperscale reference specification, not this facility design. Where it conflicts with the HLD, DLD or ICD already in the model, the ICD was treated as authoritative and the specification as supplementary.
assumptions.consequence: Instruments added from the specification may not exist at this site, and instruments this site has may still be missing. The instrument layer is therefore indicative of class and signal type, not a verified installed list.
assumptions.resolution: Verify the instrument index against the site P&ID and the loop schedule. Until then treat instrument-derived hazards as candidate findings.

assumptions.statement: The specification tags instruments singly (CT-001, TT-001, EM-002). The model has two cells and six rows, so tags were fanned out with a suffix — TT-002/1..3, EM-002 per row — and the resulting numbering does not match the source drawing.
assumptions.consequence: Cross-referencing the model against the source P&ID by tag alone will not resolve one-to-one. Any report quoting a tag must also quote the asset id.
assumptions.resolution: Adopt the site loop-numbering convention when the real instrument index is supplied, and re-key.

assumptions.statement: Zone G, the five life-safety systems and the thermal buffer were added from a generic reference architecture, not from this facility’s design documents. Quantities, locations and vendor classes are representative.
assumptions.consequence: Consequence figures derived from these assets — particularly the supply-chain and egress-lighting hazards — are indicative of the class of exposure rather than sized to this site.
assumptions.resolution: Reconcile against the facility drawings and the fire strategy at the next floor walk, then re-derive severities.

assumptions.statement: Elevator emergency phones and elevator BMS integration (reference ICD-10) are deliberately out of scope: the model is single-storey and has no elevators.
assumptions.consequence: The telephony system is incomplete against the reference by exactly one interface, and it becomes mandatory in any multi-storey Design B.
assumptions.resolution: Carry ICD-10 into Design B rather than retrofitting it here.

assumptions.statement: Grounding, lightning protection and seismic anchorage are modelled as attributes on 37 primary assets rather than as graph nodes.
assumptions.consequence: They are queryable per asset but do not appear as paths, so no threat walk or cascade can traverse them. That is intentional — they are properties, not flows.
assumptions.resolution: None. If a client needs an earthing single-line, it is a separate drawing rather than a graph layer.

assumptions.statement: The staging VLAN was described as a stub with no inward route. A walk from it reaches 293 assets.
assumptions.consequence: Read carelessly this looks like a segmentation failure. It is the internet-egress loop: staging reaches the internet for vendor images, and the internet reaches the facility through the carrier entries. The direct inward path is absent as designed.
assumptions.resolution: Stated on the asset and in N8-CY-001 verification so the figure is not misread. If the site egresses staging through a proxy with no return path, the loop closes and the figure drops.

assumptions.statement: Z6 assets are archetypes of external pathway classes, not an inventory of this facility’s actual third-party connections.
assumptions.consequence: The Z6 hazards describe the class of exposure correctly but the count, partners and protocols are representative. A real engagement would enumerate every third-party connection from the firewall rule base and the contract register.
assumptions.resolution: Replace with the actual external-connection register at the next workshop, then re-derive severities.

requirements.evidence: Each cell has its own distribution path: 2 UPS in 2N (Cell A: 9395XR + Liebert EXL; Cell B: Galaxy VXL + MegaFlex), its own RPP, and its own busway spine (PWR_cellA_busway_spine / PWR_cellB_busway_spine). Verified by cascade: a Cell A busway loss stops 67 assets and no Cell B rack, where the shared spine previously stopped 127 across both cells. A single UPS loss now stops 1 asset — the 2N pair holds.
requirements.shared_upstream: The substation, MV lineup, generators, bulk fuel and BESS remain campus-shared by design — cells share generation, not distribution.

requirements.evidence: 6 row CDUs are cell-scoped (3 per cell). The 3 chillers and 2 towers are now correctly scoped as shared central plant per WP06, not cell-dedicated.
cellA_bms_zc and cellB_bms_zc — Z2, SL-T 2-3, hold last-good setpoints if the campus BMS is lost. Campus BMS supervises but does not control.
cellA_facp and cellB_facp — Z4 addressable panels with their own detection and agent release, reporting one-way by dry contact to the campus panel. Per-row VESDA and nozzles unchanged.

Per cell: OT switch, OT firewall and protocol gateway on a cell OT VLAN with no inter-cell routing. Each cell firewall aggregates to the campus diode; deny-by-default with no cell-to-cell rules. All 18 row telemetry conduits now terminate on their own cell segment.

cell_conformance.significance: All five cell requirements are met in the topology, and each one is verified by a query against the model rather than by inspection. The OT boundary bounds a compromise to 4 assets; the power boundary bounds a busway loss to one cell. The residual exposure is the shared central chiller plant — correctly shared per WP06, and the reason N5 reconciles at 2.9x rather than the full campus multiple.
campus_shared_correctly_separated: central chiller plant and cooling towers

changes: Added per-cell OT switch, OT firewall and protocol gateway (10 new assets, 16 new conduits).
Added per-cell BMS zone controller with setpoint autonomy.
Added per-cell Z4 fire panel with one-way reporting to the campus panel.
Re-scoped the chiller plant and cooling towers as shared central plant.
Rewired all 18 row telemetry conduits from the single campus OT segment onto their own cell segment.
Declared cell membership on every asset in both graphs.
Split the hall busway spine into two cell-bounded spines with their own RPP risers.
Assigned the four UPS blocks two per cell in 2N, and connected the two that previously had no downstream path.

verified.method: Threat-path walk from each cell OT switch; cascade propagation from each cell busway and from a single UPS.
results: Cell A OT segment as entry point: 4 assets reachable, stopped at 2 boundaries (was campus-wide).
Cell A busway failure: 67 assets stopped, $720K/hour, no Cell B rack affected (was 127 across both cells).
Single UPS failure: 1 asset stopped — the 2N pair within the cell holds.
Engineering workstation: 167 assets reachable — unchanged, because that path enters through the campus IT estate, not a cell segment.

sources: 108 Datacenter Hyperscaler BOM and Attack Surface (Sections 1–17)
architecture_review.method: Every equipment category in both source inventories was checked against the model asset register. Gaps are recorded whether or not they were closed.

closed.was: Sensors reported straight to the Z2 supervisory zone controller, skipping Purdue L1 entirely.
closed.fix: Added a mechanical and an electrical DDC per cell (Saia-Burgess PCD QronoX, the only BMS DDC certified to SL-3). All 36 row sensor and leak connections rewired to terminate at the DDC tier.
closed.significance: high — a whole Purdue level was missing, which understated the attack surface and put a zone boundary in the wrong place.

closed.was: N14 (BMC firmware) carried an ALE and controls in the hazard log but had no corresponding asset in the graph.
closed.fix: Added a BMC estate asset per row (128 BMCs each, Z5, Redfish/IPMI) with management edges to all 96 racks and to the OOB console server.
closed.significance: high — a costed hazard node with nothing in the model to attach it to.

closed.gap: OT IDS had no field presence
closed.was: The Nozomi console existed but no sensors, so the model could not distinguish monitored segments from blind ones.
closed.fix: Added passive SPAN/TAP sensors per cell and at the IDMZ boundary, each one-way from its mirror port.
closed.significance: high — "operators blinded" is a recurring hazard theme; detection coverage has to be visible to be assessed.

closed.was: Rack power went busway -> rack with no intelligent PDU tier.
closed.fix: Added A-bus and B-bus switched rPDUs per row and re-parented all 96 rack power drops through them.
closed.significance: high — switched outlets are remote power control over production servers: a Z3 asset with Z0 consequence.

closed.fix: Added a redundant Tridium JACE-8000 pair reaching into both cells’ field tiers.
closed.significance: medium — the JACE runs 200+ drivers and is the highest-value single Z2 host in a real BMS.

closed.was: Aisle containment had temperature and leak sensing but no pressure differential.
closed.fix: Added a containment differential pressure transmitter per row on 4-20 mA to the mechanical DDC.
closed.significance: medium — containment bypass and recirculation are only detectable by differential pressure.

closed.gap: PTP grandmaster had no upstream reference
closed.was: Timing originated inside the facility with no external source modelled.
closed.fix: Added a roof GNSS antenna/receiver feeding the grandmaster, with Galileo OSNMA noted.
closed.significance: medium — GNSS spoofing corrupts IEC 61850 protection coordination and every log timestamp.

outstanding.note: Standard on new hyperscale campuses. Detection-only deployments are the norm; jamming is heavily regulated. No modelled consequence path, so omitted.

outstanding.gap: Visitor management system and PSIM/SOC layer
outstanding.note: A guest sign-in kiosk exists but not the VMS-to-PACS badge issuance integration, nor the PSIM that correlates perimeter alarms with automatic camera call-up.
CMDB is modelled; the ITSM platform it federates with is not. Its conduit to DCIM would be a Z0 -> Z1 crossing.
Out of scope for a zone/conduit assessment; no control authority.
Dual-use security and thermal anomaly detection. Would add a second independent temperature observation, which is a genuine safeguard against the SPOOFED hazards.
PKI is modelled but not the key custody layer beneath it. Relevant to the OPC UA and BACnet/SC certificate trust the model already depends on.

outstanding.gap: Chemical dosing skid and make-up water storage
outstanding.note: The water treatment PLC exists without the dosing equipment it commands, or the water quality instruments (conductivity, pH/ORP) it reads.
Named in the compute tray attack surface but not modelled separately. Supply-chain scope under IEC 62443-2-4.

architecture_review.systemic_note: The two most consequential findings were both structural rather than missing boxes: a whole Purdue level absent from the control path, and a costed hazard node with no asset behind it. Neither would have surfaced from counting equipment.

resolved_assumptions.statement: Electrical and cooling controls share one Purdue L2 managed switch.
resolved_assumptions.resolution: CONFIRMED as built. All FIVE legs modelled off ot_sw: protection relays, UPS network management card, chiller control, genset controller, and the six row CDU PLCs. Drove new hazard N6-CY-004 at RPN 288.

resolved_assumptions.statement: Protection relay attaches to the MV switchgear, not the GIS.
resolved_assumptions.resolution: Relay now attaches to mv_swg with sensing and trip authority. The gis → relay edge is retained as a secondary status feed rather than the primary path.

resolved_assumptions.statement: Transfer order and BMS head-end placement.
resolved_assumptions.resolution: Transfer order UNCHANGED — transformer → LV switchgear → ATS as modelled; the block-diagram order was not adopted. BMS head-end remains at Z2, not moved to Purdue L3.

resolved_assumptions.statement: EPMS is one asset or two.
resolved_assumptions.resolution: Split. epms is the ION9000 revenue meter at Z2; epms_srv is the EcoStruxure/Foreseer supervisory server that polls it and forwards to DCIM.

resolved_assumptions.statement: Clean-agent suppression had bottles and nozzles but no authorising control.
resolved_assumptions.resolution: Added the releasing panel, two hold-to-abort stations and the fourth support-area FACP. The former facp → bottles edge is replaced by facp → rel_panel (request) and rel_panel → bottles (authorise), so the discharge decision now has an owner in the graph.
